themes_detail.label: Sudden surge in street noise complaints
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 14 THIS WEEK, up 367% from the 3.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.5), suggesting a new or intensifying noise source affecting public spaces in Tottenville/Great Kills.
evidence: 14 noise complaints THIS WEEK vs 3.0 weekly baseline (367% spike)
Z-score of 5.5 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Spike is acute and recent, not sustained over months
reporting_angles: Investigate what triggered the sudden noise spike—construction, events, new commercial activity, or enforcement changes
Interview affected residents and identify specific complaint locations to map the geographic center

themes_detail.label: Mysterious spike in pet safety complaints
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK, up 700% from the 0.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.42), alongside a 3100% spike in bike/roller/skate complaints and 3100% spike in lot condition complaints, suggesting possible new enforcement activity, safety concern, or youth congregation in a specific public space.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.4 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Concurrent 3100% spike in bike/roller/skate complaints (4 complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.1 baseline)
Concurrent 3100% spike in lot condition complaints (4 complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.1 baseline)
Clustering of multiple complaint types suggests geographic concentration or behavioral pattern
reporting_angles: Locate the specific park, lot, or public space generating all three complaint types—likely the same venue
Interview NYPD, Parks Dept, and community members to understand whether this reflects a new youth activity hub, enforcement crackdown, or genuine safety hazard

themes_detail.label: Missing street signs and infrastructure decay
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK, up 500% from the 1.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.0), while curb condition complaints spiked to 8 LAST WEEK, up 482% from the 1.4 baseline, indicating accelerating deterioration of public infrastructure in this week and last week.
evidence: 6 street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs 1.0 weekly baseline (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
8 curb condition complaints LAST WEEK vs 1.4 weekly baseline (482% spike, z-score: 5.03)
Two-week sustained pattern of infrastructure complaints aligns with long-standing CB budget request for street reconstruction
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify which street segments are deteriorating fastest
Cross-reference with DOT street reconstruction requests and community board recurring budget asks for street reconstruction funding

themes_detail.label: Elevated elevator outages in residential buildings
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK, up 1100% from the 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.16), affecting residents' mobility and accessibility in multi-unit buildings across the district.
evidence: 3 elevator complaints LAST WEEK vs 0.2 weekly baseline (1100% spike, z-score: 4.16)
Spike is recent but not current (last week, not this week)
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings had elevator failures and interview residents with mobility challenges
Examine whether this reflects deferred maintenance, contractor delays, or supply chain issues for parts

themes_detail.label: Emerging homeless services demand
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints spiked 3 WEEKS AGO to 3 complaints (2300% above the 0.1 weekly baseline, z-score: 8.69), indicating potential increase in unsheltered population or service needs in Tottenville/Great Kills, though this signal is less current than other spikes.
evidence: 3 homeless assistance complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Signal is older than current-week spikes but statistically severe
Aligns with long-standing CB budget request for outreach services to vulnerable populations
reporting_angles: Connect with Department for the Aging and homeless services providers to understand whether Tottenville is seeing increased unsheltered presence
Investigate whether the spike was event-driven (weather, service closure) or reflects structural increase in demand
